generatorPage.title: Initialize Engine
generatorPage.description: Configure parameters for procedural generation. High civilization counts on smaller map sizes may result in unstable early-era boundary conflicts.

error.seed: The seed has to be a whole number, or hex like 0x7F8A9B2C.
error.size: A {size}-unit world has too little room to seat {civs} civilizations.
error.sizeAdvice: Raise the world size to at least {min}, or ask for fewer.

confirm.replace:
Replace {output}?

The file you are reusing will be overwritten with a new run of these settings through the current engine.

source.description: Change a number and generate, or run them unchanged through the engine as it stands now. The first {years} years of a longer run are the same history — the seed is deterministic.

continue.label: Continue through year
continue.description: Keeps seed {seed}, {civs} civilizations and a {size}-unit world. Writes a new file; the {years}-year export stays on disk.

modal.description: The procedural engine is currently generating tectonic structures, atmospheric conditions, and initial biological parameters for seed #{seed}.

library.title: Worlds Library
library.description: Manage and explore generated historical simulations.
library.compatibility: This viewer reads exports from schema v{min} to v{max}. A world written by an earlier engine still opens, and is labelled below with what it was recorded before — those panels are empty rather than wrong. Anything older than v{min}, or written by a newer engine than this viewer, is marked unreadable and has to be run again.

error.deleteConfirm:
Permanently delete {name}?

This cannot be undone. The file will not be moved to trash.

loading.endStateError: Could not read the end of this history.

empty.message: No generated worlds yet. The first completed run will appear here.

actions.run: Run {name} again through the current engine

details.noRecipe: No generation recipe. Use the original CLI command.

schema.tooOld: schema v{version} · too old to read

schemaSummary.current: Schema v{version} — everything this viewer can show.
schemaSummary.older: Schema v{version}, written by an earlier engine. It opens, but it was recorded before {count} later addition{additions} to the export, so those panels stay empty. Run the seed again to get them.
schemaSummary.tooNew: Written by a newer engine (schema v{version}); this viewer reads up to v{max}. Update the viewer, or open it with the engine that wrote it.
schemaSummary.tooOld: Schema v{version} predates the oldest export this viewer can read (v{min}). Run the seed again through the current engine.
schemaSummary.unreadable: This file does not declare a schema version, so it is not a world export the viewer can read.

groupTitles.values: What it was governed by, year by year

figureLife.arcCaption: The whole life, retrospectively — the panels below show only what was known in the year selected. Bar height is how much the chronicle recorded in that year, counting what it marked notable for three; the number beside each turn is the {measure} it happened at, and its colour is what the turn was about. Click anywhere on the strip — or focus it and use the arrow keys — to move the year.
figureLife.constellationCaption: Line weight is how much the bond carries; solid is kin, dashed a companion, dotted a rivalry. Only people living in {year} are drawn — move the year and watch the lines go out.
figureLife.significanceCaption: How much of the recorded history runs through this person, not how good a person they were. Most lives sit near the left, which is what makes the right worth finding.

cosmology.Cosmic timeline description: From the Big Bang to the year the Chronicle opens. Lookback dates are measured from Year {year}.
cosmology.Star scale description: The star is drawn at that same scale — its full disc would be {width}× the width of this strip. Bodies smaller than a pixel are drawn as a dot; hover for exact figures.

account.afterWar: , beginning in {year}. The comparison uses dated passages and their references; it does not grade the text's accuracy. Service totals can summarize engagements that have no individual description.

historiography.continuationSections: Coverage including the earlier passages. Added passages:
historiography.oneSummarizedEngagement: This engagement appears in the service summary.
historiography.manySummarizedEngagements: {count} of these appear in the service summary.
historiography.copyingNote: Copying dates below are not new dates of authorship. A later copy does not make the original account later. The record does not say which continuations reached each copy.

disposition.intro: Their own inclinations, on the dials their people hold.
disposition.cultureWithReligion: 's reading of each: everyone is rolled around the values they were born to, then pulled toward what
disposition.cultureWithoutReligion: 's reading of each: everyone is rolled around the values they were born to, so the gap is the person rather than the people.
disposition.afterReligion: teaches, so the gap is the person rather than the people.
disposition.centralism: Centralism is rolled around what the office itself invites rather than around a culture, so it carries no tick.
disposition.independence: Independence is how far they let their people govern them: a follower stays near the ticks, a rebel answers with their own inclinations.
disposition.noTitles: Recorded for everyone, though it only ever governed anything for those who came to rule.

worldMap.harbourNote: Anchors sit in the water a harbour was founded for, not on the town. A wave marks a river landing.
worldMap.houseNote: A banner is the throne; a house mark is where the line rose. Focus a realm to see where that house's living members reside. Residence is recorded as of the chronicle's end.
worldMap.tradeNote: Dashed amber is overland demand, blue uses river access, teal the coast. Weight is traffic in {year}. These are logical links; the road under one, where there is one, is drawn separately.
worldMap.roadNote: Solid brown is a way worn between two towns; pale stone is one bridged and paved. Only land routes whose traffic held up for long enough are ever roaded, and a road stays on the map after the trade that paid for it has gone.
worldMap.nothingRecorded: Nothing was recorded in this year.
worldMap.noHouseOnThrone: No house held a throne this year.

houseAtTown.other: {count} members of the house live at {town}

worldMap.noFaithPreached: Nothing was preached anywhere in the world this year.
worldMap.roadTitle: {road} of {name}, cut in {built}{paved} · {length} units of made way{abandoned}

knowledge.title: Knowledge
knowledge.emptyWorld: Nobody in this world wrote down a reading of anything. Observation needs a comet somebody lived to see twice, and a scribe in the town that saw it.
knowledge.subtitle: What people said about the world, and what became of the saying
knowledge.sightingsHint: Written down, and the evidence every measured reading rests on
knowledge.realmsHoldingHint: Realms that ever held one of these readings
knowledge.inWritingHint: Works that set a reading down, so it could outlive whoever had it
knowledge.noTransitions: This export was written before the engine recorded where a reading travelled, so nothing below can say who came to hold one, what carried it, or when it was let go. The readings themselves are all here. Run the seed again for the rest.
knowledge.columnExplanation: Columns say what could settle a thing, not how right anyone was. Doctrine is permanently unanswerable by the sky and is never graded here — a mythic reading is a held position with its own patrons, not a wrong answer.
knowledge.practiceNotRecorded: Practice — what could actually be done — is not a record this engine writes yet, so it has no column.

columnNote.Observation: What was written down, and what was derived from it. The sky can answer it.
columnNote.Practice: What could actually be done. Answered by the object or the harvest, never by a proposition.
columnNote.Doctrine: What was believed about why. Nothing settles it, and nothing here grades it.

verdict.Untested: The year they named lies beyond the record
verdict.NotTestable: Not a thing the sky could answer

knowledge.noReadingReachedYear: No measured reading named a year the record reached.
knowledge.moreInTable: and {count} more in the table above.
knowledge.register.measured: Measured — it states a number the sky can meet or miss
knowledge.register.mythic: Mythic — it says what the light is for, which nothing measures
knowledge.nothingWrittenAsEvidence: Nothing written down — it was not that kind of reading
knowledge.nothingCarried: Nothing carried this reading anywhere. It stayed with whoever set it out.
knowledge.skyMadeOfIt: What the sky made of it
knowledge.noVerdict: A verdict is what happened in the sky, not what anybody believed. This one has none.
knowledge.claimantDidNotHear: {name} did not live to hear it.
knowledge.refutedExplanation: The sky answering says nothing about who went on holding it. Whoever kept teaching this after that year is below, and is not wrong for it.
knowledge.verdictExplanation: What the sky settled and what anybody believed are separate records. Nothing on this page grades a held position.
knowledge.noRealmHeld: No realm is recorded as having held it.
knowledge.holdingExplanation: Having a reading and holding with it are two facts. A realm can keep one it argues with, or shelve one the sky confirmed.

independent: {name} made a home at {place} after leaving the old seats behind.
{place} became their ground, chosen rather than inherited.
Having gone out, {name} put down roots at {place} on their own terms.
deep: {name} spent most of their life rooted in {place}.
{name} rarely strayed far from {place}, where the record first found them.
Familiar places and established ways remained important to {name}, above all at {place}.
tied: {name} remained closely tied to {place} for much of their life.
{name} kept returning to {place} as though their life had never truly left it.
The town at {place} shaped {name} more than any office their years later brought.

loyalty: {name} and <<friend>> stood by one another for {years} years, a tie the record never forgot.
Through {years} years, {name} kept faith with <<friend>> when lesser ties cooled.
<<friend>> remained at the centre of {name}'s life for {years} years — loyalty the chronicle could name.

mentor: {name} passed down what their trade had taught them to <<other>>.
Much of what <<other>> knew came through {name}'s teaching.
{name} shaped <<other>>'s path as a mentor the record still names.
apprentice: {name} learned the craft under <<other>>, and carried it forward.
What {name} became owed a great deal to <<other>>'s instruction.
<<other>>'s teaching left a lasting mark on {name}'s life.

killing: {name}'s quarrel with <<rival>> ended in blood the record could not soften.
Violence between <<rival>> and {name} closed a feud that had long been gathering.
{name} and <<rival>> settled their grievance at the edge of a blade.
feud: {name} carried a long quarrel with <<rival>> through the public life of the record.
A feud with <<rival>> shadowed {name}'s years more than any single battle.
{name} and <<rival>> remained locked in a dispute the chronicle followed for years.

success: {name}'s ventures on the road returned with gain the record could count.
Mercantile work rewarded {name} more often than it failed them.
failure: {name} repeatedly sought their fortune through trade, though little of it endured.
The road took more from {name}'s ventures than it ever gave back.
Trade occupied {name} for years, but the record remembers more loss than gain.

discovery: {name} wrote down a sighting at {place} the record had not held before.
What {name} saw in the sky stayed in the chronicle when others let it pass.
The first record of that apparition is in {name}'s hand.
life: {name} lived among books, observations, and the work of making sense of them.
Learning ran through {name}'s life — not as ornament, but as habit.
The record remembers {name} as one who studied, copied, and kept what others let pass.

pilgrimage: Faith led {name} to {place} on pilgrimage, and the journey stayed in the record.
{name} sought the holy at {place}, and the chronicle kept the road.
Pilgrimage to {place} marked {name}'s devotion in a way office alone could not.
office: {name} served the faith in office, and the record treated that service as their life's spine.
Religious duty shaped {name}'s public years more than trade or arms.
{name} held the faith's work close through the offices their life accumulated.

religiousScholarship: {name} joined religious office to scholarly habit — doctrine learned and kept.
The record shows {name} as both servant of the faith and student of its teaching.
{name} read, served, and copied within the same devout life.
consolidation: {name} gathered power into their own hands rather than leave it scattered.
Office after office, {name} made authority personal.
The record shows {name} bending institutions toward a single will.
institutionalService: {name} served the institutions of the realm long and faithfully.
Public office defined {name}'s mature years more than private ambition.
{name} held posts the chronicle could list and did not hurry to leave them.

conspiracy: {name} plotted against authority the record later exposed.
Conspiracy marked {name}'s years when office alone could not satisfy them.
{name} turned from subject to conspirator when power closed its doors.
denied: {name} resented the offices passed to others and did not hide it.
Being passed over left a wound in {name}'s public life the record followed.
{name} chafed under authority that never quite admitted them.

frontier: {name} made a life at the edge of the known world, settling at {place}.
Migration brought {name} to {place}, and there their story stayed.
{name} left the old seats behind and rooted anew at {place}.
territorialAmbition: {name} pressed outward — in war, office, and the reach of their ambitions.
The record remembers {name} on campaign and in command more than at rest.
Territory and victory mattered to {name} in a way peace alone never could.
isolation: {name} kept apart from the centres where others sought favour.
Distance and independence marked {name}'s path more than courtly tie.
{name} lived at a remove from the seats that shaped most lives around them.

turned: {name} turned on <<other>>, and the record did not forget who broke the tie.
Faith with <<other>> ended when {name} broke it.
{name} betrayed <<other>> — a wrong the chronicle kept.
suffered: <<other>> turned on {name}, and the record named the broken faith.
{name} was betrayed by <<other>>, a wound the chronicle still carries.
The tie with <<other>> ended in betrayal that shadowed {name}'s later years.

interpretation.fallback: {name} lived in a way the record can name through {theme}.
